 Inox Wind Admits Missing Earlier FY27 Growth Target, Shifts Focus To Balance Sheet Strength
 The company had previously indicated that it was targeting approximately 75% revenue growth and EBITDA margins of 20–22% for the current financial year.
 Manish Kumar 
 16 Nov 2026 09:47 IST
 Follow Us
 Inox Wind Admits Missing Earlier FY27 Growth Target, Shifts Focus To Balance Sheet Strength Photograph: (AI)
 Inox Wind has withdrawn its earlier revenue growth expectation of around 75% for FY27, acknowledging that it will not achieve the target as the company shifts its focus towards equipment sales, cash flow generation and balance sheet strengthening. During its Q2 FY27 earnings conference call, the company's management clarified that it would not meet the revenue growth expectations indicated in the previous quarter. However, it refrained from providing a revised revenue guidance for FY27.
 Advertisment The company had previously indicated that it was targeting approximately 75% revenue growth and EBITDA margins of 20–22% for the current financial year. Responding to an analyst's question on the earlier guidance, management acknowledged that the company would not achieve those numbers, attributing the revision to its strategic realignment towards equipment supply and the decision to prioritise business quality over revenue growth.
 Advertisment "We'll not reach those numbers," management said, adding that the company had consciously decided to recalibrate its growth trajectory to improve its balance sheet and ensure better-quality cash flows. The company is now targeting revenue of approximately ₹7,500 crore in FY28, with an EBITDA margin of around 20%. Management described this as a conservative target, indicating that there could be an upward bias to the revenue outlook.
 Strategic shift towards equipment supply 
 A key reason behind the revised growth expectations is Inox Wind's decision to increase the share of equipment supply in its third-party order book to approximately 75%, compared with 61% as of October 2026. The company is reducing its dependence on turnkey engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) projects, which typically involve higher working capital requirements and greater exposure to project execution and payment delays.
 Advertisment Management said the transition has involved foregoing certain business opportunities and discontinuing some orders, which has affected its near-term revenue trajectory. It added that pursuing higher revenue through turnkey projects could have increased receivables and working capital requirements, weakening the company's balance sheet.
 During the earnings call, management highlighted that it did not want to continue financing customers' projects through delayed payments, particularly where customers hold back 20–30% of project payments for extended periods.
 Advertisment The company is instead prioritising equipment supply contracts and customers with better payment records, including group companies, to improve cash flow visibility. As of October 2026, Inox Wind had an order book of approximately 3.8 GW, providing execution visibility of more than 24 months. Its order inflows stood at approximately 1.85 GW during H1 FY27, including around 350 MW secured during Q2.
 Advertisment Management expects growth momentum to continue in H2 
 Despite withdrawing its earlier FY27 growth expectation, Inox Wind said it expects business momentum to improve in the second half of the financial year. Management indicated that the company is seeing a sequential improvement in revenue and expects this momentum to continue through Q3 and Q4 FY27.
 However, it declined to provide a specific revenue growth number for the remaining quarters, citing the ongoing transition in its business model. The company also expects debtor days to decline to below 150 days by the end of FY28 as it strengthens collection efficiency and working capital management.
 Commodity inflation adds to margin pressure 
 Apart from the strategic realignment, Inox Wind also reported pressure on its margins during Q2 FY27 due to higher commodity and raw material prices, partly attributed to geopolitical tensions in West Asia. The company reported consolidated revenue of ₹1,378 crore in Q2 FY27, registering a sequential increase of 58%. Adjusted EBITDA stood at ₹238 crore, while EBITDA margin was approximately 17%.
 Management said fresh bids and incremental contracts are being priced dynamically to reflect the prevailing commodity cost environment, which should support margin normalisation as these orders move into execution.
 It also clarified that the reported EBITDA did not reflect the full contribution of Wind World's 4.5 GW wind operations and maintenance (O&M) portfolio, acquired by Inox Green Energy Services. Had the contribution been recognised, the consolidated EBITDA margin would have been around 20%, according to management. The Wind World portfolio will be consolidated into Inox Green's financials from Q3 FY27.
 ₹7,500 crore revenue target for FY28 
 Looking ahead, Inox Wind is targeting revenue of approximately ₹7,500 crore in FY28, with an EBITDA margin of around 20%. The company expects the growth to be supported by a higher share of equipment supply, commercialisation of its next-generation 4.45 MW wind turbine platform, expansion of transformer manufacturing and entry into higher-value products such as inverters, electronic control systems and unit substations.
 The increased contribution from Inox Green following the consolidation of acquired O&M portfolios is also expected to support consolidated profitability. Management said the company would review and reaffirm its FY28 outlook towards the end of Q4 FY27. The revised growth trajectory marks a shift in Inox Wind's priorities from pursuing higher revenue growth to improving profitability, reducing working capital intensity and generating sustainable cash flows.
